default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-328.title: Overnight tug-of-war micro-break fade
E-328.hypothesis: Lou/Polk/Skouras: overnight and intraday returns pull in opposite directions because individuals push prices overnight while institutions trade during the day against that flow. When the last few sessions' overnight returns sum clearly one way, intraday institutions lean against it, so short-term breaks in the overnight direction are faded (up-breaks sold after overnight gains, down-breaks bought after losses).

E-329.title: Unextended initial-balance micro-break fade
E-329.hypothesis: Dalton: while the session has not yet extended beyond its initial balance (first 30-90 minutes), the opening institutions' range is holding and the day is still in balance, with responsive traders at both IB edges; short-term breaks inside the IB are small pushes they absorb, so fade them until the first range extension.

E-330.title: Rushed-approach micro-break fade
E-330.hypothesis: A break of the window high reached by a traverse of the whole window from its low within a few bars is a burst of urgent market orders that emptied the book on the way up; the burst is the move and it arrives at the level spent, while the resting offers above remain, so the break reverts; fade it (mirror).

E-331.title: Open-VWAP conflict micro-break fade
E-331.hypothesis: When price sits between the session open and a clearly separated session VWAP, the two most-watched intraday references give opposite verdicts: open-anchored day traders and VWAP-anchored desks take opposite sides, so neither camp follows a short-term break and the other absorbs it; fade breaks in that conflicted zone.

E-332.title: Open-inside-prior-value micro-break fade
E-332.hypothesis: Dalton: an open inside yesterday's value area that stays accepted there signals a balance day in which yesterday's extremes usually hold and responsive traders dominate; while the session opened and still trades inside yesterday's volume-weighted value band, short-term breaks lack an initiator and are faded.

E-333.title: Opposite-push conviction fade
E-333.hypothesis: Compare the size behind the two ends of the window: a close through the window high on a bar trading much less than the bar that set the window low means the down push had more conviction than the up break; the heavier participant is still on the other side and leans on the light breakers; fade (mirror).

E-334.title: Seasonal deep-book minute micro-break fade
E-334.hypothesis: At times of day when volume per point of range (20-session same-minute medians) is high next to the session average, the book is deep: many contracts trade for little price change because liquidity providers quote size; a short-term break at those minutes pushes into refilled depth and reverts.

E-335.title: Decelerating-approach break fade
E-335.hypothesis: If the window's closes rose but the latest third rose less than the one before (negative curvature), buying pressure is fading as price arrives at the high; the break is the last small push of a slowing move, the parent order behind the rise is finishing, and the late breakout buyers are the exit; fade (mirror for a decelerating fall).

E-336.title: Thin-book session micro-break fade
E-336.hypothesis: When today's range per contract traded so far is far above its usual value at this minute, the session's moves are being made by small orders through a thin book rather than by size; such impact-driven moves overshoot and liquidity providers who re-quote pull them back, so short-term breaks on such sessions are faded.

E-337.title: WIN price at the dollar's session extreme hold
E-337.hypothesis: The WIN price printed when WDO set its latest session high (low) marks the index level at the peak of the day's risk-off (risk-on) flow, where foreign desks finished hedging; when WIN later returns to it and closes back on its side, those desks defend the level instead of adding, so trade away from it.
